articles.title: Man City lodges ‘comprehensive’ appeal after guilty verdict in financial rule-breaking scandal
articles.summary: Manchester City has lodged a “comprehensive” appeal, the club confirmed Friday, following the publication of a report by an independent commission detailing large-scale financial rule-breaking by the Premier League giant in one of English soccer’s biggest scandals.
articles.body: Manchester City has lodged a “comprehensive” appeal, the club confirmed Friday, following the publication of a report by an independent commission detailing large-scale financial rule-breaking by the Premier League giant in one of English soccer’s biggest scandals. “The club’s firm position,” read a short statement from City, “is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe.” City has protested its innocence throughout the long-running case, which dates back to 2018 and reached a milestone Tuesday, when the Premier League published a verdict saying the Abu Dhabi-controlled club was “guilty of all charges related to serious breaches” of the competition’s financial rules from 2009-18. City has yet to receive a punishment. According to the Premier League, potential sanctions could be a reprimand, fine, points deduction or, in the worst case, expulsion from the competition. No team has ever been expelled from English soccer’s top flight. City officials said they would lodge an appeal and that was filed on Thursday evening, the club said, ahead of Friday’s deadline. “The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case,” City said, using language from previous statements on the case. Premier League regulations state that the chair of the three-person disciplinary commission that found against City now has to appoint a new appeal board. That also will consist of three people, one of whom “shall have held judicial office,” the league’s rules state. The appeal board will then schedule a hearing that should finish within 12 weeks after the appeal is filed, and cannot exceed five consecutive days. That will be addressed in a separate, confidential hearing with the commission and there has been no word whether sanctions can be imposed before the decision of the appeal is reached. The Premier League has only said its intention is that the process is concluded “as soon as possible.” City was found to have systematically broken the Premier League’s financial rules for nearly a decade in what the competition’s chief executive, Richard Masters, described as the most significant disciplinary case in the league’s history. The investigatory panel found that City artificially inflated its revenue — using what the league has called “sham” commercial deals — by more than $1 billion from 2009-18 to circumvent financial fair-play rules that restricted rival clubs, and allowing City to buy some of the best players in the world. That was the foundation of a long and unprecedented period of success in which City changed the landscape of the world’s most popular soccer league, with the northwest club winning eight league titles from 2012-24. City committed almost all of the 115-plus violations, the commission found: 80 from 2009-18 for alleged financial misdeeds and another 35 from 2018-23 for allegedly not cooperating with the investigation. Source of sponsorship could be focus in appeal City is likely to focus part of its appeal around the issue of how its Abu Dhabi-based sponsorship deals were funded. The commission found that sponsors in Abu Dhabi only paid 119.25 million pounds ($158.4 million) of the 949.94 million pounds ($1.26 billion) stated in club accounts, with the remaining 830.69 million pounds ($1.1 billion) being paid by the Abu Dhabi United Group, the private company of Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan that bought City in 2008. Sheikh Mansour is a member of the United Arab Emirates’ ruling family. City contended that “no part” of the deals were funded by the ADUG and that, instead, the Abu Dhabi government — which owned the sponsors — had helped to fund the deals “from time to time.” And so in City’s opinion, that source of extra funding was misunderstood, the commission wrote. The panel rejected that explanation by City as untrue, concluding it was “concocted well after the event” to disguise the source of funding. In an internal video to City staff — obtained by broadcaster Sky News — City chief executive Ferran Soriano said: “The whole Premier League case against us is based on a single false accusation: that the owner’s personal money was somehow and secretly put into the club via some sponsors from Abu Dhabi. This is just not true.” On Friday, the Football Association — the governing body of soccer in England — expressed concern that the “integrity” of the game had been affected by the scandal. In its first reaction to the case, the FA said: “The independent commission’s decision has significant implications for the integrity of the game. We are carefully considering the decision and its implications and will take action where appropriate.” The FA added that it would “continue to monitor developments closely” and would not comment further because proceedings were ongoing. The City case is currently a soccer disciplinary proceeding, not a criminal investigation. On Thursday, a cross-party committee of lawmakers called on Britain’s tax authority to assess the case. The chair of the Treasury Committee, Dame Meg Hillier, wrote to the permanent secretary of Her Majesty’s Revenue and Customs (HMRC), saying: “While I acknowledge that taxpayer confidentiality may inhibit what you can disclose, I would welcome reassurance from HMRC that you are seized of the importance of these issues and the public interest in the case.” In another example of the widespread impact of the scandal involving City, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has been repeatedly asked his view on the issue. On Wednesday, Burnham said he would be “really concerned” to lose City’s ownership from English soccer, saying they had been a “huge partner in the building of modern Manchester” and of City as a global force, while also saying he was not getting involved in the process. Burnham was formerly the mayor of Manchester. On Thursday, Downing Street sought to clarify that the prime minister viewed the ruling as “serious and there can’t be any suggestion that anyone is above the rules.” “If wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the appropriate consequences,” Burnham’s office said in a statement, which stressed that the independent process was ongoing.

articles.title: Manchester City Files Appeal After Being Found Guilty of Premier League Financial Breaches
articles.summary: Manchester City announced Friday that they filed an appeal regarding the Premier League's determination that they were guilty of more than 100 charges related to financial violations.
articles.body:
Manchester City announced Friday that they filed an appeal regarding the Premier League's determination that they were guilty of more than 100 charges related to financial violations.

"Manchester City Football Club can confirm that at 7 p.m. on Thursday, Oct. 1, 2026, the club lodged its comprehensive appeal against the opinion of the Premier League Commission, in relation to the Premier League disciplinary matter," the statement read. "The Club's firm position is that, on multiple grounds, the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe.

"The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. We will continue to respect due process and are necessarily restricted in what we can say further until all proceedings are complete."

The Premier League announced Tuesday that it had found Manchester City guilty of numerous breaches of the league's financial rules, alleging that the club misled the Premier League regarding its financial situation in myriad ways, including devising "sham" contracts with commercial partners.

As part of their findings, the Premier League noted that the violations in question occurred from 2009 to 2018 and saw Manchester City artificially inflate their commercial revenue by £830 million, which equates to $1.08 billion.

The Premier League has to announce any punishments against Manchester City, and that may continue to be the case as the appeals process plays out.

Manchester City is one of the most successful clubs in Premier League history with 10 titles in English soccer's top division.

Their greatest dominance occurred from 2014 until the present day with eight of their Premier League titles being won from 2014 to 2024.

City won four titles in a row from 2021 to 2024, and six out of seven from 2018 to 2024.

The Sky Blues also won their only UEFA Champions League title during that stretch, accomplishing that feat in 2023.

While City fell short of Premier League titles each of the past two seasons, they remain top contenders, as they finished third in 2025 and second in 2026.

Through five matches this season, Manchester City sit atop the Premier League standings with 15 points thanks to five wins, no losses and no draws.

articles.title: Once bitten, twice shy: How Kolkata is gearing up for India vs Brazil after Lionel Messi fiasco
articles.summary: TimesofIndia.com in Kolkata: With just over 24 hours until the India vs Brazil match, the Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata was brimming with activity on
articles.body: TimesofIndia.com in Kolkata: With just over 24 hours until the India vs Brazil match, the Salt Lake Stadium in Kolkata was brimming with activity on Friday, despite it being a national holiday. Cleaning was underway in large numbers, and hoardings were being put up throughout the gigantic stadium and inside. Around 4 p.m., the Brazil national team walked out for a light practice session.After a brief chat by the coaches, including manager Carlo Ancelotti, the squad underwent some limbering exercises and running about to test agility. It was followed by a rondo comprising the entire squad. In another corner, the goalkeepers were tested with low efforts as they dove around on the warm, upgraded turf of the iconic stadium.Just 20 hours back, the five-time World Cup champions Brazil had landed in Kolkata from Australia. A tight security cordon was placed as they exited the VIP gate and a convoy ensured they swiftly made their way to a plush five-star hotel. There, too, an unbreachable security bandobast kept a large group of fans at bay.Much has changed since Lionel Messi's chaotic, and short, visit to this part of the world in December. But the memory lingers and has proven to be a warning for all involved.For the security officials and organisers, nothing is being left to chance. Pilot cars, barricades at a distance, and layers of security have been the mantra. As they made their way from the airport to the hotel, an eight-minute window was worked out. As the Seleção left the team hotel, some fans did get a glimpse of the team but were largely kept at arm's length.The other side of the warning went to fans. Some of the football enthusiasts are believed to have been scared off by the disorder of the Messi visit, where angry fans breached security and a 22-minute appearance disappointed many.Another reason for fans staying away has been the ticket prices. 24 hours before kick-off, the ticket prices began from Rs 3,500 and went up until Rs 15,000. Even when they were offered at discount, not many takers have shown up. 14,000 tickets were offered at a reduced price to supporters of East Bengal, Mohun Bagan and Mohammedan Sporting, but all were not taken up. As per the last report, only 30-40% of the tickets have been sold so far for the marquee fixture.Lack of starpower in the current Brazil team is another factor. Vinicius Jr., who plays for Real Madrid, is the biggest face involved. Barcelona's Raphinha returned to Spain after sustaining a right thigh injury during a friendly win against the Socceroos.Big occasion for KolkataBrazil and Argentina both have dedicated fanbases in Kolkata, where the fans' love for their flamboyance goes back decades. Neighbourhoods get draped in the colours of Brazil and Argentina during World Cups. Salt Lake Stadium had sold-out crowds of more than 60,000 when Argentina played a friendly in 2011, and Brazil competed in the U-17 World Cup six years later.At the airport, there was little to hint that one of the biggest football teams on the planet had arrived just a few hours ago. A cabbie informed that they exited from Gate 3C and were quickly on their way.Few kilometres away as one headed into the city towards the Salt Lake Stadium, a giant hoarding read: 'Bumper Saturday' bearing the faces of India goalkeeper Gurpreet Singh Sandhu and Brazil's winger Vinicius Jr.We know how this region loves the national team... we are happy to be here to play against India"We know how this region loves the national team... we are happy to be here to play against India," Ancelotti said on Friday. "All these games... are good preparation and a good opportunity to show what we can do."I would like the players to enjoy themselves, to play with happiness in every game. You want to play with joy. It's not a test, but an opportunity," continued the Italian.Captain Marquinhos said the friendly was a way to thank Brazil's supporters in India."Of course, the focus is always very much on playing well and winning the match, but being here is also a way of thanking the Indian people for their support and for following the Brazilian national team all these years, throughout its history," he said."This is also the second-largest group of supporters of the national team outside Brazil, so it’s a pleasure and an honour."Even bigger occasion for Khalid's IndiaWorld No. 138 India are the lowest-ranked opponents Brazil have faced since 1998, when they played 185th-ranked Andorra.The gulf in quality and achievements is massive between the two teams. With India failing to qualify for the 2027 Asian Cup, and missing the Asian Games completely on account of not meeting the Sports Ministry's qualification requirements, the contest is as much about the test as it is about the spectacle.AIFF president Kalyan Chaubey called this a 'historic' opportunity, while the federation hopes this contest can attract new followers and give Indian players an experience they rarely get. But it has come at a cost.India withdrew from the inaugural FIFA ASEAN Cup, a competition featuring some of the teams at par with India. Instead, with the two competitions clashing, and an attempt to use two teams being disallowed, the friendlies have been given the priority.Defender Anwar Ali underlined the importance of not getting overawed. “We just have to focus. Because everyone knows how Brazil play. So, we just have to keep calm in the field. And deal with the pressure,” he said.In a conversation with TimesofIndia.com, former captain Bhaichung Bhutia questioned that move, arguing that competitive matches and long-term investment would offer greater value than spending heavily on a high-profile friendly.The Khalid Jamil managed side are coming on the back of a gritty 1-1 draw against Panama in Bengaluru on September 25. But the next challenge is even bigger."They are the best team. They are known as the best of the best. They are defensively very strong. Their attacking is good,” Jamil said in the press conference.SquadsIndia: Goalkeepers: Albino Gomes, Gurpreet Singh Sandhu, Prabhsukhan Singh Gill, Som Kumar; Defenders: Abhishek Singh Tekcham, Akash Mishra, Anwar Ali, Bijoy Varghese, Hmingthanmawia Ralte, Jay Gupta, Pramveer, Ricky Meetei Haobam; Midfielders: Anirudh Thapa, Ashique Kuruniyan, Farukh Choudhary, Lalengmawia Ralte, Macarton Nickson, Mohammed Sanan, Ricky Shabong, Sahal Abdul Samad; Forwards: Edmund Lalrindika, Irfan Yadwad, Manvir Singh, Rahim Ali, Ryan Williams, Vikram Partap Singh.Brazil: Goalkeepers: Hugo Souza, Pedro Morisco, Otavio; Defenders: Arthur Dias, Douglas Santos, Gabriel Magalhaes, Jair, Marquinhos, Matheuzinho, Mauro Junior, Vitor Reis, Wesley; Midfielders: Andrey Santos, Breno Bidon, Bruno Guimaraes, Danilo Santos, Douglas Luiz, Gabriel Bontempo; Forwards: Endrick, Stephen, Joao Pedro, Pedro, Rayan, Samuel Lino, Vinicius Junior.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Petty or justified? Erling Haaland sues airline over post made during World Cup featuring his blonde ponytail
articles.summary: Erling Haaland is suing Norwegian Air Shuttle for using an edited image of his iconic blonde ponytail in a World Cup marketing post, claiming a breach of his rights.
articles.body: Erling Haaland is taking Norwegian Air Shuttle to court over a marketing post published during the 2026 World Cup that featured a distinctive part of his image. The airline’s social media campaign showed an aircraft carrying the blonde ponytail that had become closely associated with Haaland during his stellar run with Norway, despite the striker having since cut his famous hair short. The post was later removed, but the use of Haaland’s recognisable image has now become the subject of a legal dispute.Haaland's legal team says the airline used his distinctive characteristicsAccording to Aftenposten, the case centres on an alleged breach of marketing law after Norwegian published a social media post featuring an aircraft digitally edited with blonde hair tied into a ponytail, resembling Haaland’s former hairstyle. The post carried the caption, “We’ve never looked more Norwegian,” before being deleted by the airline.Haaland and York Promotions Ltd filed the lawsuit through the law firm Schjodt, with the case now set to move towards an initial digital planning meeting at Oslo District Court on October 9.Haaland’s lawyer, Thomas Hagen, confirmed the legal action in an email to Norwegian tabloid newspaper Verdens Gang.“We confirm that, on behalf of York Promotions Limited and Haaland, we have filed a lawsuit against Norwegian Air Shuttle ASA,” Hagen said.He said the dispute concerns what Haaland and his representatives consider to be an unlawful use of the striker’s “distinctive characteristics” to market flight tickets during the football World Cup.The lawsuit does not appear to have been accompanied by a publicly detailed financial claim, with the precise amount of damages or compensation being sought not publicly specified in the material surrounding the case.Norwegian says it was supporting the national teamNorwegian has confirmed that it received the lawsuit, although the airline says it does not understand why the legal action has been brought.Eivind Hammer Myhre, a duty media officer for Norwegian, said the company viewed the post as part of its support for Norway during the World Cup rather than an attempt to make an unlawful commercial use of Haaland’s identity.“It is true that we have received a lawsuit, we do not understand the reason for it,” Myhre said.“Like most Norwegians, we took part in supporting the national team this summer, through a few spontaneous posts based on trends popular on social media.”Myhre said the airline regarded the lawsuit as an unfortunate response to what it described as expressions of support for Norway’s players.“It is unfortunate that cheers of support were met with a lawsuit, but we hope for a sensible dialogue so that in the future we too will be allowed to continue supporting our shared sporting heroes,” he added.The next formal step is scheduled for October 9, when representatives of the two sides are due to take part in a digital planning meeting at Oslo District Court.Haaland's former hairstyle became part of the disputeThe airline’s post referred to an appearance that Haaland himself had already moved away from by the time the dispute emerged.On August 23, 2026, the Manchester City forward cut his long blonde hair into a short, military-style buzz cut, bringing an end to the hairstyle that had become closely associated with his public image.Haaland revealed the change in a viral vlog published on YouTube and across social media, accompanied by the caption, “Short hair don't care.”He had grown the long hairstyle since 2021, wearing it in different forms including a ponytail and man-bun during his rise to global prominence with Manchester City and Norway.In the vlog, Haaland explained that he had been considering cutting his hair since Norway’s World Cup campaign ended in July, when the team reached the quarter-finals before losing 2–1 to England.He ultimately waited until the eve of the 2026/27 domestic season before making the change, describing the haircut as part of a “fresh start”.Haaland had played a central role in Norway’s run to the World Cup quarter-finals, making the hairstyle used in Norwegian’s deleted social media post particularly recognisable to supporters.The legal dispute now turns on whether the airline’s use of those recognisable characteristics crossed the line from social media support for the national team into unlawful marketing, a distinction that articles.summary: Firmó un repóker con la Sub-21 y hoy, nada más aterrizar en Ibiza, la llamada de la Absoluta le hizo cambiar el rumbo hacia la península. En clave Real Madrid, se postula como recambio de un Mbappé tocado ante el Villarreal
articles.body: Un billete de lotería premiado, una herencia inesperada, un pleno a quince... pocos golpes de fortuna igualan al vuelco que ha dado la vida de Carlos Espí en apenas unos meses. Solo que lo suyo no es azar, sino gol. El ariete valenciano no ha venido al Real Madrid a hacer bulto, y lo lleva demostrando desde que aterrizó. Allá donde pisa, deja huella en forma de tanto. Para medir el vértigo de su ascenso conviene mirar atrás. Hace nada, Espí militaba en el Levante, donde se consagró como una de las perlas de La Liga hasta ser elegido mejor sub 23 de la competición. De las canteras de Alzira y el Levante saltó al Bernabéu el pasado 30 de julio, reclamado por Mourinho como ese '9' rematador que el técnico ansiaba. Bastó una llamada que Carlos no pudo contar ni siquiera a sus amigos. Y una vez de blanco, no ha necesitado más que retazos para dejar su sello. Porque en los escasos minutos (26) que ha sumado esta temporada desde el banquillo ha convertido en oro cada aparición, con dos goles y otro anulado que valieron puntos. Esa pólvora la trasladó también a la Sub 21 aprovechando el parón, en lo que era su estreno con la categoría. En el primer partido ante Finlandia no se le dieron las cosas, pero frente a San Marino salió de inicio y arrasó por Serravalle con un repóker de época, cinco tantos que lo encaramaron a lo más alto de la tabla de goleadores de la fase, solo por detrás de Gonzalo, que suma seis pero en nueve partidos. El propio Espí habló con asombro y los pies en el suelo. "Nunca me imaginé meter cinco goles con España. Es inexplicable, no soy consciente de lo que estoy haciendo", confesó a la RFEF. "Me ha cambiado la vida por completo de un verano a otro. Ha sido un inicio de temporada muy bueno, he metido dos goles que han podido ayudar al Real Madrid y ahora quiero ayudar al máximo a la Sub-21". Palabras de quien no pierde el norte pese a que todo le sonría. Y lo que le sonríe no cesa, porque ese repóker ha servido de pasaporte a la Absoluta. Este mismo viernes, Luis de la Fuente lo ha convocado con los 'mayores' para suplir al lesionado Ferran Torres, baja por molestias en el tobillo, de cara a los duelos de la Nations League ante Chequia y Croacia. De hecho, Espí había aterrizado en Ibiza con la Sub 21procedente de Rimini (Italia) cuando le llegó la llamada, y tuvo que cambiar de rumbo hacia la península para presentarse con la Absoluta, que pone rumbo a Oviedo. Ese torrente de buenas noticias tiene, además, un destinatario atento en Valdebebas. Porque Mourinho tendrá que hacer encaje de bolillos para el partido ante el Villarreal, con Mbappé entre algodones tras caer lesionado en el primer duelo de Francia en este parón, precisamente mientras marcaba un gol. Mientras la referencia gala se resentía, su posible recambio se destapó a lo grande a unos cientos de kilómetros. Si Mbappé no llega a tiempo, el valenciano ha dejado claro que la caña sigue cargada, y que a Mou no le temblaría el ataque confiándole el '9'. Una buena noticia para un Madrid que no quiere tropezar de nuevo con errores del pasado en lo que a recuperación de lesiones se refiere. El chaval ha hecho los deberes; ahora le toca al técnico decidir si le pone nota de titular.

articles.title: Man City owners cannot 'retain status' if guilty verdict stands after appeal, says Gary Neville
articles.summary: Gary Neville gives his verdict on the charges being levelled at Manchester City and questions whether, should a guilty verdict be upheld after appeal, the club's owners can continue to operate in the Premier League
articles.body:
The club confirmed on Friday that it has lodged a "comprehensive" appeal to refute the guilty verdict handed down by an independent commission, detailing large-scale financial rule breaking over a nine-year period.

City have protested their innocence throughout the long-running case, which dates back to 2018 and reached a milestone on Tuesday, when the Premier League published their determination that the club were "guilty of all charges related to serious breaches".

According to the Premier League, potential sanctions could include a fine, points deduction or, in the worst possible case, expulsion from the competition.

But Neville, a co-owner of Salford City in the EFL, says the only appropriate course of action would be to review whether City's owners adhere to the regulatory vetting laws set out by the league, adding their alleged actions have "dragged English football through the mud".

Neville said: "It's hard to see how the Man City owners can comply with the owners' and directors' test in this country if the verdict remains.

"The reality is, because of improper owners of clubs, there are a lot stricter rules in place. It'll be difficult for the Man City owners to retain their status.

"Clubs are protected assets, community assets, because of the meaning of them to fans and people of a city, so owners have to comply with the rules and laws set out in the test.

"The only appropriate punishment is to apply the owners' and directors' test, firstly, and then to look at the achievements over the period and determine whether they should still stand.

"Those two things would have the most direct consequence on English football. If I was Man City, I'd snap your hand off for a fine or points deduction, even if it was 60 points, because that would only damage you for a moment in time.

"To own a football club in this country is one of the greatest responsibilities you can have. It needs to be taken very seriously.

"We can't get bogged down with fines and points deductions, concentrate on the two most important things: the achievements during that time and what happens to the owners and executives who oversaw that period."

The investigatory panel found that City had artificially inflated its revenue, using what the league has called "sham" deals, by more than £900m to circumvent financial fair-play rules.

That then allowed City to buy some of the best players in the world in a period where they dominated English football's biggest prizes.

Neville added: "The Premier League is our greatest export around the world, and now it's being dragged through the mud because the very best team over the last 15 years, as we stand, are guilty of winning titles inappropriately. That's devastating.

"If the guilty verdict stands it won't be real. It'll be a period tainted forever. The achievements themselves are tarnished."

articles.title: Thomas Tuchel: England boss would 'never rule out' selecting players in lower divisions
articles.summary: England boss Thomas Tuchel says he would "never rule out" selecting someone who is not playing in the top flight, should Manchester City be relegated.
articles.body:
England boss Thomas Tuchel says he would "never rule out" selecting someone who is playing outside the top flight for their club, should Manchester City be relegated as punishment for breaching financial regulations.

On Tuesday, it was confirmed that City had been found guilty by an independent commission of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial rules between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

The club, which denies guilt, has appealed against the verdict, saying the ruling contained "clear material errors, of law, principle and fact and is unsafe".

The sanctions for City have not yet been decided but potential punishments include expulsion from the league, points deductions and fines.

The current England squad includes City players Elliot Anderson and Marc Guehi, while Nico O'Reilly was in the group until he left with an injury.

How Gordon became one of England's main men

England are preparing to play Croatia in the Nations League in Rijeka on Saturday (17:00 BST).

Speaking to the media on Friday, Tuchel said the City verdict was a "big subject" in the England camp.

Asked if he would select players not playing in the top flight, the manager said: "There is always a possibility.

"I would always try to pick the best team for the camp, for the occasion, for the tournament.

"I will never rule out that because they don't play in the top flight in their country. We need to look at it case by case."

All 24 players in the current England squad play in top leagues for their clubs and it is very unusual for a player to represent the Three Lions if they are not in a top division.

However, James Trafford was in Tuchel squads in March and June 2025 while still in the Championship with Burnley, but he was an unused substitute on those occasions and did not win a full cap until he returned to Manchester City.

Goalkeeper Sam Johnstone was the last player to represent England while playing in the Championship, for West Brom in 2021, while Kalvin Phillips - then at Leeds - made his debut for England before he had played in the Premier League.

Asked about his players discussing the City verdict, Tuchel said: "We had some time off between the matches and it is a big subject. Everyone speaks about it, so there is no other voice needed

"I am glad to be not that voice. No-one needs my half knowledge on the topic.

"Of course, the players talk about it. City players talk about it. We talk with them but only briefly.

"They are ready to go tomorrow, that's what they show on the pitch and in camp. But of course, it's a big topic in the camp."

articles.title: Canales y Chupe, novedades en la Sub 21 para la 'final' ante Rumanía
articles.standfirst: El combinado de David Gordo incorpora a los dos jugadores de cara al decisivo encuentro del martes en Can Misses, con el que España puede sellar su billete al Europeo
articles.summary: El combinado de David Gordo incorpora a los dos jugadores de cara al decisivo encuentro del martes en Can Misses, con el que España puede sellar su billete al Europeo
articles.body: La selección española sub-21 afronta con dos novedades la recta final de la fase de clasificación para el Europeo de 2027. David Gordo ha incorporado a Peio Canales y a Chupe para el decisivo encuentro del martes ante Rumanía, que se disputará en Can Misses (Ibiza) y en el que a España le basta una victoria para certificar el primer puesto sin depender de otros resultados. Canales ya había formado parte de la sub-21 en esta misma fase de clasificación, por lo que regresa a una dinámica que conoce. Para Chupe, en cambio, será la primera vez que vista la camiseta del combinado nacional en la categoría. Los internacionales se sumarán a la expedición a la mayor brevedad posible para incorporarse a la preparación del choque. Este viernes, por la tarde, la Selección realizará su primera sesión de trabajo en el estadio balear, que presentará lleno para la final ante los rumanos.

articles.title: Luis García no descarta fichar un sustituto de Antoniu Roca
articles.standfirst: Se teme que el extremo cedido por el Espanyol pueda estar de baja más de cuatro meses
articles.summary: Se teme que el extremo cedido por el Espanyol pueda estar de baja más de cuatro meses
articles.body: El entrenador del Mallorca, Luis García, no ha descartado la posibilidad de incorporar a un futbolista por la lesión de larga duración del extremo catalán Antoniu Roca, quien se espera que pueda estar de baja más de cuatro meses. "Cuando lo hablemos se decidirá", ha dicho en la rueda de prensa previa al enfrentamiento ante el Girona del próximo domingo, en el que ha remarcado: "Como siempre, el club trata de buscar lo mejor, no hemos hablado de nada y cuando nos sentemos a hablar, se decidirá qué se hace". Ante la ausencia de Manu Morlanes por su lesión en el tobillo, García ha resaltado los pocos goles encajados hasta la fecha: "En los últimos cinco partido recibimos solo un gol, para tener tantos jugadores ofensivos. Creo que tenemos bastante equilibrio a pesar de no tener ese medio tan defensivo, somos de los equipos menos goleados de la categoría", afirmó. El equipo ha digerido ya la derrota ante el Almería y se centra en mejorar la versión ofrecida: "Ha sido una semana con muy buen ambiente, nivel de exigencia muy alto e incidiendo en temas a mejorar de donde venimos. Muy focalizados, preparados, hemos trabajado de manera sobresaliente y queda todavía un día para matizar", señaló. Sobre su próximo rival, García ha puesto en valor la reacción del equipo al "difícil mercado de traspasos" que vivieron: "El Girona ha tenido un mercado muy difícil y ya está en situaciones de eliminatorias de ascenso. Se enfrentan dos muy buenos equipos, va a ser un partido muy bonito para el espectador", destacó. El partido estará marcado por la ausencia del ex bermellón Mateu Morey en el cuadro catalán por la 'cláusula del miedo' incorporada en el traspaso: "No lo sabía, me enteré porque me lo dijeron del cuerpo técnico. Seguro que a Mateu le fastidia, pero si juega y mete gol nos matáis. Son cosas que se negocian entre clubes e interesantes para nosotros", añadió.

articles.title: La prórroga dorada de Szczesny
articles.standfirst: Hace dos años que el meta salió de su retiro para firmar por el Barça y ha logrado 5 títulos
articles.summary: Hace dos años que el meta salió de su retiro para firmar por el Barça y ha logrado 5 títulos
articles.body: Hace dos años, el 2 de octubre de 2024, el Barcelona anunciaba que había alcanzado un acuerdo con Szczesny para incorporarlo a su plantilla después de la grave lesión de Ter Stegen. El guardameta polaco, que se había retirado del fútbol profesional unos meses antes y ya se encontraba viviendo en España, decidió volver a ponerse los guantes para defender la camiseta azulgrana. Lo que inicialmente parecía una solución de emergencia terminó convirtiéndose en una etapa especialmente positiva para el portero, que, a día de hoy, puede presumir de haber conquistado cinco títulos con el conjunto catalán. Szczesny firmó inicialmente hasta el final de aquella temporada, con el objetivo de suplir a Ter Stegen. Sin embargo, su rendimiento y, sobre todo, su influencia dentro del vestuario dejaron un buen sabor de boca en el club. El Barcelona decidió entonces prolongar su contrato hasta 2027, ampliando así una aventura que el propio futbolista no parecía tener entre sus planes cuando anunció su retirada. Durante su primera temporada como azulgrana, el polaco disputó 28 encuentros y tuvo un papel importante en los éxitos del equipo. En la campaña siguiente pasó a desempeñar un rol más secundario, como portero suplente, ya que el Barcelona firmó a Joan García. Y, en el presente curso, parece haber quedado relegado a la tercera posición en la jerarquía de guardametas de Hansi Flick. Aun así, su importancia dentro del vestuario va mucho más allá de los minutos que acumula sobre el césped. Su experiencia, personalidad y liderazgo le han convertido en una figura respetada y querida por sus compañeros. La trayectoria de Szczesny también permite poner en perspectiva lo que ha supuesto esta inesperada prórroga. A lo largo de su carrera profesional, el guardameta ha conquistado 11 títulos, cinco de ellos desde su llegada al Barcelona. Con la camiseta azulgrana ha levantado dos Ligas, dos Supercopas y una Copa del Rey. Su historia en el Barcelona, por tanto, se ha convertido en una especie de prórroga inesperada, pero, a la vez dorada . Lo que comenzó como una llamada de emergencia tras la lesión de Ter Stegen terminó dando paso a una etapa en la que Szczesny ha vuelto a competir al máximo nivel y ha ampliado considerablemente su palmarés.

articles.summary: Falta peligrosa para el Real Madrid. Estaba bien colocado Astralaga para despejar el remate de Leiva. Buena jugada individual del delantero que bate a
articles.body:
Última hora del Real Madrid Castilla - Atlético Madrileño en directo:

¡¡¡MUUUUUUYYYY BUEEEENAAASS TARDEEEEESSS!!! Día de derbi de filiales. Real Madrid Castilla y Atlético Madrileño se ven las caras a las 21:15 en el Alfredo Di Stéfano. Los locales acumulan una racha de tres partidos sin conocer la victoria . Derrota y empate como visitante frente a Águilas y Sant Andreu respectivamente, sumados al triunfo del Alcorcón en el campo merengue. Tan solo una victoria en lo que llevamos de temporada para los de Julián López de Lerma, lo que ha provocado que ocupen la decimocuarta posición, a un punto de los puestos de descenso.

Por su parte, el Atlético Madrileño lleva dos partidos sin llevarse los tres puntos, desde su enfrentamiento con el Murcia. Empate contra Huesca y derrota contra Villarreal B. En este último partido, el conjunto de Fernando Torres acabó con nueve futbolistas , después de que Javier Gil y Marc Domènech fueran expulsados por roja directa. Ocho puntos en la clasificación, tres más que el Castilla, lo que hace que estén en la séptima plaza, a uno de los playoffs de ascenso.

¿Quién se llevará los tres puntos? Te lo contamos aquí, en MARCA.

articles.body:
Última hora del Bélgica - Turquía en directo:

Seguimos con la tercera jornada de la UEFA Nations League con dos selecciones que no llegan en su mejor memento, sobre todo la Turquía de Arda Güler . Los otomanos llegan tras perder sus dos primeros partidos de la edición, ante Francia (0-1) y una goleada ante una Italia en horas bajas (1-4) . De hecho, hubo pitos en la derrota ante la 'Azzurra', agrandando una situación poco amable para un equipo que llega, además, de ser una de la decepciones del Mundial.

Bélgica , por su parte, convenció en la primera jornada ante Italia (0-2) , pero ante un rival de la entidad de Francia (llena de suplentes), se le vieron las costuras (0-1) . Eso sí, los 'Diablos Rojos' tienen jugadores con los que ilusionarse, con Mika Godts , jugador del PSG, siendo de lo más destacado del conjunto belga. Hoy, de nuevo en casa, buscarán el camino de cuartos para despué, intentar levantar su primer título desde 1920, cuando ganaron la medalla de oro en los Juegos Olímpicos de Amberes.

No queda nada para que ruede el balón en el Stade Maurice Dufrasne (Lieja) . ¡Vaaaaaamos!

articles.title: Francia - Italia en directo | Última hora de UEFA Nations League en vivo hoy
articles.summary: Doue recorta dentro del área, le pega y tapona Kayode. Kean intenta salir a la contra, pero Kalulu le cierra el camino y es falta En la segunda jugada
articles.body:
Última hora del Francia - Italia en directo

¡¡¡Muy buenas noches, familia de MARCA!!! El azar ha querido regalar un guiño cargado de épica para los verdaderos apasionados del fútbol. Zinedine Zidane afronta su esperado estreno como seleccionador francés nada menos que ante Italia, la misma escuadra frente a la que disputó su último choque vestida de corto en aquella inolvidable y convulsa final del Mundial de Berlín 2006. Un reencuentro con aroma a revancha y nostalgia que mide a la prometedora era de Zizou con la segunda etapa de Roberto Mancini al frente de la Azzurra .

El impacto del técnico marsellés en el banquillo galo no ha podido ser más efectivo, firmando un arranque impecable con dos victorias a domicilio en el Grupo A. Francia se impuso con oficio en Turquía gracias a un solitario tanto de Kylian Mbappé --quien cayó lesionado en ese mismo choque-- y repitió idéntico guión (0-1) en el estadio Rey Balduino frente a Bélgica, esta vez con Michael Olise asumiendo los galones para dictar sentencia. Seis puntos de seis posibles que respaldan el inicio de una transición ambiciosa tras los 14 años de mandato de Didier Deschamps.

Por su parte, la Italia de Mancini desembarca en este duelo inmersa en una fase de reconstrucción que ha despertado una renovada ilusión en el país transalpino, a pesar de firmar un bagaje de una de cal y otra de arena. Tras tropezar en el debut ante Bélgica (0-2), la Azzurra firmó una brillante exhibición ofensiva para golear a Turquía (1-4), sumando tres puntos que la mantienen en la pelea directa.

Llega la hora de la verdad. Noche de fútbol del bueno, de de toda la vida con dos colosos del fútbol mundial frente a frente y el morbo añadido de ver a Zidane dirigiendo sus primeros minutos en suelo francés. ¡Arrancamos con la previa y la mejor cobertura en directo en MARCA.com !

articles.title: Barcelona see 20-year-old Premier League striker as a future target; remain in contact with his camp
articles.summary: With FC Barcelona scouring the market for a new centre-forward this past summer, the name of Eli Junior Kroupi of AFC Bournemouth emerged as a potential targ...
articles.body:
With FC Barcelona scouring the market for a new centre-forward this past summer, the name of Eli Junior Kroupi of AFC Bournemouth emerged as a potential target.

The 20-year-old French forward was coming on the back of an impressive debut campaign in the Premier League and was seen as a good, long-term fit by the Blaugrana .

As it became clear that Julian Alvarez would not arrive, the Catalans even contacted his representatives to explore the possibility of a move .

However, at the end of July, he suffered a fracture to the fifth metatarsal in his right foot, ending any hopes of a transfer.

Now, according to SPORT , Kroupi remains highly regarded by part of Barcelona's sporting department, which is convinced that the Frenchman has the potential to become a top-level player.

Barcelona rate Kroupi very highly. (Photo by Jack Thomas/Getty Images)

As such, the Catalan club will continue monitoring him once he returns from his injury. The forward is now entering the final stage of his recovery and is expected to make his comeback within a month at the latest.

As per the report, Kroupi was considered an option for Barcelona when it became increasingly clear that Alvarez would not be joining.

Much of the sporting department backed the young forward, while president Joan Laporta also liked the idea , despite an asking price of around €100 million and the risk involved in investing such a significant amount in a 20-year-old.

The striker's his style of play is seen as something that fits extremely well with the type of forward that Deco and Hansi Flick wanted for the team. The injury ultimately brought negotiations to a halt.

Still in touch with his camp, but competition expected

Kroupi is currently recovering from an injury. (Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty Images)

But, Barcelona have continued to maintain contact with Kroupi's representatives in order to remain well positioned.

The La Liga champions still believe he could be an excellent investment, despite Bournemouth making it clear that they will not sell for less than €100 million.

However, competition for his signing could ramp up as Arsenal and Tottenham remain interested in the player and could even attempt to sign him as early as January.

For now, Barcelona are not planning an immediate operation. Instead, the youngster is viewed as a potential future signing, from the summer of 2027 onwards.

articles.title: El Sevilla se rinde a Unai Emery en la previa del XV Trofeo Antonio Puerta
articles.standfirst: El técnico posó en el césped junto a las tres UEFA Europa League y algunos ex jugadores
articles.summary: El técnico posó en el césped junto a las tres UEFA Europa League y algunos ex jugadores
articles.body: Unai Emery regresaba al Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán esta noche para la disputa del XV Trofeo Antonio Puerta. "Un honor", dijo el ahora técnico del Aston Villa en la previa. Antes del partido, y con las tres UEFA Europa League que consiguió en el banquillo blanquirrojo alineadas en el césped, el de Hondarribia recibió el aplauso cerrado de una afición que no olvida los momentos de gloria que vivió con Emery, que dirigió a los andaluces entre enero de 2013 y junio de 2016. No estuvo solo. Jesús Navas, Coke, Diogo, Javi Varas, Negredo, Fazio Nico Pareja, Sergio Rico y Vicente Iborra, algunos de los jugadores que estuvieron a sus órdenes en el Sevilla, le acompañaron en este reconocimiento. Navas le hizo entrega de un cuadro conmemorativo con la icónica imagen de Emery besando un trofeo de la Europa League. Además, los videomarcadores del estadio mostraron un emotivo vídeo con los mejores momentos de aquel Sevilla campeón de tres UEFA Europa League, así como algunas de las frases más reconocidas de unos de los técnicos más laureados de la historia del club. "Porque nadie la quiere como nosotros".

articles.title: Man City appeal: Club's strategy brought into question by 2015 statement main sponsor Etihad Airways submitted to US government
articles.summary: Man City were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission; City deny all charges and have lodged an appeal against the verdict; City were charged by the Premier League with more than 100 breaches in February 2023
articles.body:
Sky Sports News understands that City are expected to argue as part of their appeal that the extra funding for their sponsorship deals came from the Abu Dhabi government and not the club's majority owners, Abu Dhabi United Group (ADUG).

However, a statement Etihad submitted to the US Departments of Commerce, Transportation and State in May 2015 appears to contradict this explanation.

"The assertion that the Abu Dhabi government paid for Etihad's sponsorship of English Premier League football club Manchester City is equally false," Etihad's submission read.

"In 2011, Etihad and Manchester City entered into a 10-year sponsorship agreement, which included naming rights for Manchester City's stadium.

"Etihad funded this sponsorship from its own liquidity. It is not uncommon for airlines to have sponsorships with sports teams and their venues."

The 60-page filing from 2015 is a response by Etihad to claims that it received market-distorting state subsidies. Etihad, whose sole shareholder is the Abu Dhabi government, added later in the submission: "We are government-owned and have been since our founding.

"We are and have always been clear that we do not receive any subsidies from the Abu Dhabi government, and that we are financed through a combination of equity, shareholder and commercial loans.

"Our shareholder's equity and loans are not subsidies under any applicable definition; they are the means by which the Abu Dhabi government has sensibly invested in a successful business model."

An independent disciplinary commission this week found that City broke financial rules by disguising £830m of owner funding as sponsorship income for nine seasons between 2009 and 2018.

City's lawyers are already believed to have put forward the defence at the original 2024 hearing that the extra funding was provided by the Abu Dhabi government and not the owners despite the links between the two.

This explanation was rejected by the commission in the judgement that was published on Tuesday. The three-person panel "concluded it was an explanation that the club had concocted well after the event in an attempt to conceal the realities of the Disguised Funding Scheme".

City's defence that the extra funding was funded by the Abu Dhabi government was something they argued was not the case during their Court of Arbitration for Sport hearing in Lausanne when they appealed against their two-year ban for breaking UEFA's financial fair play rules.

Witness evidence at that hearing from former Etihad Airways chief executive James Horgan stated that sponsorship obligations to City had been paid "out of Etihad's own funds".

Could Man City's appeal could drag into 2027?

Sky Sports News' Kaveh Solhekol and Amar Mehta :

Manchester City's appeal could drag on into next year if they argue that the process should not be run according to Premier League rules which were introduced for this season.

City have filed their appeal and the new rules about appeals state that this part of the disciplinary process has to be concluded within 12 weeks and the appeal hearing can last no longer than five days.

City's lawyers could argue that they were charged in 2023 and a hearing was held in 2024 - when the rules about a speeded-up appeals process were not in the Premier League Handbook.

A legal expert told Sky Sports News Manchester City would have a strong case for arguing that the new rules should not apply in this case.

The new rules were introduced to ensure that clubs, where possible, were punished in the same season as relevant rule breaches.
